text:
A: Hiya! Oh, hello, can you hear me alright? I'm never sure with these things.
B: Yeah, loud and clear. Alright?
A: Yes, good thanks! I'm Joanne, I'm in Taunton. Did you manage that puzzle thing? I was all fingers and thumbs.
B: Lee. Bridgwater. Puzzle was alright, last couple did my head in a bit though.
A: Bridgwater! Oh, I was born in Bridgwater, me. My dad worked out at Hinkley for years, the old station, you know.
B: Yeah? Don't get me started on Hinkley, mate. Rent on my place has gone up twice in two years 'cos of all the workers coming in. Landlord knows he can get it, do you know what I mean? Though to be fair a couple of the lads I went school with are on proper money out there.
A: Oh, it's sort of swings and roundabouts, isn't it. And the traffic on the M5 by you, honestly, I sat there forty minutes last week.
B: Junction twenty-three's a joke. What d'you do then?
A: Erm, well, nothing at the moment really, which sounds awful. I was a veterinary nurse for over twenty years, head nurse at the end, but my back went and the shifts were killing me, so I stopped about three years ago. I help out at a cat rescue now, few hours a week. Sorry, that's a lot!
B: Nah, you're alright. What's up with your back then?
A: Lower back, it's been on and off for years. Lifting Labradors onto tables doesn't help, you know!
B: Slipped disc, me. Four years back. Used to do five-a-side, can't now. Some mornings I can barely get out the van.
A: Oh, you poor thing. What is it you do?
B: Mechanic. Independent garage out on the industrial estate, MOTs and that. Lot of bending under bonnets, so, yeah.
A: Oh gosh, that's not ideal with a back. Do they look after you there?
B: Look after me? Boss pays sod all for what we do. I'm the one finding the faults the main dealers can't, and he's sat in his office. I'll do my own thing in a couple of years, mobile mechanic, then I don't answer to no one.
A: Well, good for you. You'd have people queuing up, I bet. People are always wanting someone they trust with their car.
B: That's it. Half the time customers have been fobbed off somewhere else before they get to me.
A: My Martin's hopeless with ours. He's a surveyor, he can tell you everything about a damp wall but not where the oil goes!
B: Ha. Classic.
A: Have you got any pets? Sorry, I always ask, it's the nurse in me.
B: Diesel. Staffie cross. He's sat here now actually. Chewed the remote again this morning.
A: Oh, bless him! They do love a remote, I think it smells of your hands, that's the thing, it's comforting. Mine's Biscuit, Border terrier, he's an old grump. Won't go out if it's raining, just stands on the doorstep looking at me like it's my fault.
B: Diesel'd go out in a hurricane. Take him along the river most nights.
A: Do you go up the Quantocks? I love it up there when my back lets me.
B: Sometimes weekends, yeah. Mostly it's Carnival I'm counting down to though. November.
A: Oh, Bridgwater Carnival! I haven't been in years, we used to go every year as kids. Are you in it?
B: Know a few in one of the carts. I help out with the generators and the lights and that. Proper mental how big they are now, thousands of bulbs.
A: Oh, that's lovely though, isn't it? That's proper community, that is. I might have to drag Martin along.
B: You should. Get there early, mind, parking's a nightmare.
A: I'll remember that! Sorry, I've been waffling on, haven't I?
B: Nah. Better than sitting here in silence.
A: That's true! Oh, I think we've only got a minute left.
